title: cost-normalized-quality-frontier-customer-corpora-memo-may2025
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working memo capturing an experiment series that attempts to place quantized model variants on a single cost-normalized quality frontier using anonymized customer corpora (three distinct verticals). Goal is pragmatic: give product + SRE a clear recommendation for routing policy thresholds (when to prefer FP8, INT8-GPTQ, AWQ, or fallback to full-precision) under real traffic mixes and token-cost constraints.

High-level summary findings (TL;DR)
- Under real customer corpora we saw two regimes: quality-critical queries (long-form generation and instruction-following) where FP8/GPTQ hybrids outperform AWQ by a measurable margin on QA/EM and semantic-fidelity metrics; and high-volume short inference queries (snippets, classification) where INT8/AWQ yield large cost wins with negligible customer-visible quality loss.
- When normalized by per-token cost (taking infra + kernel throughput into account) a mixed routing policy that uses AWQ for <32 token contexts and FP8/GPTQ for >=32 tokens recovers ~22–28% cost vs full-precision while keeping a quality delta within our alerting thresholds for 87% of the corpus.
- Kernel-selection noise (different implementations of the same quant format) causes up to 12% latency P95 jitter and produced correlated small quality aberrations; we need kernel fingerprinting in the profiler to pin down noisy paths.

Experimental design
---
Datasets (anonymized customer corpora)
1) Support-faqs: short Q/A pairs, avg token length 18, high volume, sensitive to factual recall (EM/QA metrics).
2) Compose: instruction-heavy customer content generation, avg token length 120, sensitive to coherence and instruction-following (ROUGE-L and semantic-similarity).
3) Search-snippets: embedding/semantic rank tasks, avg token length 45, moderate sensitivity to subtle embedding drift (cosine drop measured).

Model variants profiled
- baseline-fp16 (reference)
- fp8-optimized (our recent fp8 kernels + layernorm stability tweaks)
- int8-gptq (GPTQ quantized weights, baseline kernels)
- awq-int8 (AWQ-style quant pack + our AWQ kernels)
- hybrid-gating (runtime that can switch to fp16 for selected layers at runtime — prototype)

Kernels tested (matrix)
- vendor-kernel-a (vector lane tiling, memory-prefetch)
- open-kernel-b (streaming-friendly, lower peak mem)
- our-opt-kernel-c (blocking tuned for small-batch long-context)
We exercised all model+kernel combos.

Traffic mixes and scenarios
- steady-state bulk: 10k qps scaled across small tokens and long tokens with real interpolation from corpora.
- bursty-start: forced cold-starts/warmup every 10s to replicate customer-burst behavior.
- worst-path: corner-case prompts designed to trigger attention-sparsity and long KV cache thrash (from field reports).

Metrics captured
- Quality: ExactMatch/QA F1 (support-faqs), ROUGE-L and embedding cosine similarity vs fp16 baseline (compose, search-snippets), and a small human-eval rubric for hallucination severity (30-sample spot-check).
- Perf/Cost: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, memory footprint, per-token infra cost (normalized across GPU types used in test cluster).
- Stability: variance of latency across runs, kernel hot-path changes, quantization failure rate (NaNs, overflow).

Normalization approach
- Per-token cost = (GPU cost per second / tokens/sec) + estimated kernel overheads. GPU cost used public cloud sticker for multi-tenant cluster (we used conservative number to model enterprise pricing).
- Quality penalty = relative drop in metric (e.g., ROUGE-L delta or cosine similarity delta) vs baseline-fp16 aggregated per-corpus with a weighted scheme favoring Compose for semantic metrics and Support-faqs for EM.
- We plot cost on x-axis and 1 - quality-penalty on y to visualize frontier.

Key experimental observations
---
1) Customer-corpora sensitivity differs dramatically: Compose is the tightest constraint. For Compose, AWQ-int8 lost ~6.3 ROUGE-L points vs fp16 and produced a visible increase in incoherent completions in the human spot-check. GPTQ variants mitigated most of this (delta ~1.2 ROUGE-L) at 1.1x higher cost than AWQ but still ~0.6x cost of fp16.

2) Short-form traffic is economical with AWQ: Support-faqs saw <0.8% EM drop with AWQ-int8 compared to fp16 while per-token cost fell by ~58% (kernel throughputs favored AWQ on small-batch, low-latency paths). This strongly suggests default AWQ routing for high-QPS short queries.

3) Kernel choice matters more for latency than for quality in many cases. The same quantized weights on vendor-kernel-a vs open-kernel-b changed p95 by up to 12% and tokens/sec by ~9% depending on batch shape; quality deltas were small for these kernel swaps (<0.5% on aggregated metrics) but observable on corner prompts.

4) Hybrid-gating prototype (select layers at fp16 at runtime) closed ~60% of the quality gap between AWQ and fp16 for Compose, at a moderate throughput cost. This gating adds complexity but looks promising for a middle-tier offering (dedicated customers who care about quality and cost).

5) Warmup/cold-start patterns: quantized models recover accuracy after a few tokens, but warmup penalties (latency spikes) are more pronounced for certain kernels during cold prefixes. For bursty workloads this drove higher p99s; caching warm contexts at the routing layer mitigated most of it.

Anomalies / surprising failures
- We saw rare NaNs (~0.02% of requests) for int8-gptq on vendor-kernel-a when sequence length crossed 1.5x typical; trace points to a tiling wrap bug under a specific attention alignment. Filed JIRA-RT-7891.
- AWQ-int8 on open-kernel-b produced small but reproducible semantic drift for several Compose prompts that contain nested instruction templates. Hypothesis: quant packing interacts with merged attention bias terms; need microtests.

Practical routing recommendation (proto)
---
Given cost and quality targets asked by product (<=15% quality delta aggregate, maximize cost savings):
- Route Support-faqs and Search-snippets to AWQ-int8 by default (fast path) with a fallback to int8-gptq if kernel failure rate >0.1% in last 10k requests.
- Route Compose to fp8-optimized or int8-gptq depending on customer SLA: for customers on Standard tier use int8-gptq with fps-capacity knob; for Premium use fp8-optimized or hybrid-gating when latency budget allows.
- Add a token-length-based threshold: if prompt >= 32 tokens favor fp8/gptq. If <32 tokens, AWQ-ok.
- Add kernel-fingerprint telemetry to detect noisy kernels and trigger circuit-breaker -> switch to alternative kernel implementation.

Operational runbook items (short term)
- Implement kernel fingerprint in profiler (trace id -> kernel impl + kernel version) and add alert if p95 jitter >10% vs 1-hour moving baseline. (Evan)
- Add automated microtests for nested-instruction templates under AWQ packing to reproduce and isolate drift. (Miguel)
- Prototype a lightweight hybrid-gating config that can be toggled per-customer and instrument its token-cost regressions. (Sofia)

Data artifacts and reproducibility
- Bench harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/142 (contains traffic replay scripts and corpus split logic)
- Repro scripts live under infra/bench-scripts in our repo; they rely on anonymized corpus blobs stored in S3 (access controlled).

Open questions and next experiments
- Does per-layer selective fp16 during generation reduce hallucination risk systematically across other customers (not just Compose)? Need an N=10 customer vertical sweep.
- Can we further squeeze AWQ kernels for long-context by changing prefetching/block sizes? This may reduce its quality gap on Compose.
- How stable are these frontiers across GPUs (A100 vs H100 vs future accelerators)? We need a 3-way comparison for retail pricing sensitivity.

Notes to reviewers / items for product discussion
- The cost-normalized frontier shows room for a tiered routing policy that recoups 20–30% cost with limited customer-visible regression in most verticals. Product should weigh complexity of per-customer hybrid-gating vs offering dedicated fp8-optimized models.
- For immediate rollouts we can default to AWQ for short queries (largest impact) and gate Compose changes behind opt-in.

Appendix: quick artifact checklist
- Raw perf CSVs: s3://bench-results/may2025/cost-frontier/raw-*.csv
- Aggregated plots (cost vs 1-quality): confluence:CONFL-469
- Human eval notes: google-sheet:HV-EVAL-0525

Problems and TODOs (working list)
- [ ] Re-run worst-path on H100 and compare kernel p95 jitter (priority high)
- [ ] Add automatic fallback mechanism for kernel NaN detection
- [ ] Finalize routing thresholds and ship a canary to 10% traffic for one week

References and related tickets
- JIRA-RT-7891 (NaN tiling wrap)
- PR#142 (bench harness changes)
- Slack thread #runtime-quant: message-5732 (field report from customer X)

End of memo

(Informal notes: this doc is a working capture of bench runs and conversations. Numbers are preliminary — do not forward externally until we surface a final slide deck.)
